items.excerpt: Grant revocation and delayed effect observation Study run The version-checked transaction and the serialized receipt agree on 4 schedules. An observation after revocation finds the valid earlier commit. Cached permission admits 2 unauthorized effects when the grant changes or expires before commit. Scope · Ordered local fixture with a shared database and owner. Grant revision, commit tick and observation are distinct. The comparison leaves distributed control and production enforcement open. Matched terms: cached, permission, write, grant, before, commit

Matched terms: cached, permission, write, grant, commit, transaction

Grant at commit and delayed observation Evidence passage The effect at tick 1 used the active grant. A later observation of that journal row after revision 2 did not invalidate the earlier write. Both checked transactions withheld a write after expiry or revocation. Scope · Four ordered schedules in a shared local database under one operator. A partitioned remote sink, production enforcement, and distributed failure behavior remain outside the comparison. Matched terms: write, grant, commit, transaction, check

Disposition and observed effect Study run All 7 controls passed, including a held case with one wrong effect. The stricter scorer changed 0 historical hold labels. The 160 pairs cross four authored task fixtures with forty conditions per task, so the closure counts describe this design. The wrong-effect case is an isolated instrument control. Both status paths use one simulated journal and clock. In a separate local check, an old failure with the current response tick causes a second commit without deduplication. A trusted source revision prevents that retry in the authored case. Matched terms: still, before, commit, check

results.query: If a status read is stale but a separate projection has the right revision for an earlier write, must the client retry the write to finish review?

items.excerpt: Matched access through one or two endpoints Study run · Measured under stated conditions Primary-only status verified 48 of 288 paired cells. The two routes with second-projection access each verified 80. They agreed on disposition in all 288 cells. The gateway used 288 caller requests and 130,128 status payload bytes. The additional endpoint used 480 caller requests and 75,960 bytes. Scope The paired cells repeat four authored tasks. Status services run in separate processes under the same owner and receive controlled projections of the same starting operation journal. The protocol supplies trusted revision and known availability states. The comparison measures local IPC and logical observation costs. Separately administered outages, production time, incident frequency and human effort remain open. Matched terms: statu, read, separate, projection, revision, retry

A fresh second projection closes an already committed request Paired case · Authored paired case Conventional status: hold. Additional endpoint: closed · verified closure. One endpoint with matched access: closed · verified closure. Scope One authored review-metadata case with an exact prior effect and a non-deduplicating receiver. It illustrates a condition, not the frequency of that condition. Matched terms: statu, stale, projection, review

Crossed receiver study Study run · Measured under stated conditions Conventional status closed 128 of 160 matched cases. The added read closed 144. All 16 extra closures occurred with stale or unavailable conventional status, a fresh second read, and no receiver deduplication. Both workflows closed 32 cases each when both observations were fresh. Scope Both reads use one simulated SQLite journal. The measured difference concerns evidence availability under logical time. Production isolation, incident frequency, and human effort are open. Its original safe-hold label used commit count without testing the identity of a lone committed effect. The separate effect-score run checks that distinction. Matched terms: statu, read, stale, separate, retry

Absolute floor and equal memoization Study run · Measured under stated conditions The shared copy-09 failure routed to a specialist. Both workflows matched the expected route at 66 scripted checkpoints and each read 75 evidence documents. The serialized handoff wrote 2367 bytes. Both caught a missed invalidation when the index next returned the current revision. Scope Eleven profiles each use two consumers and three logical ticks. The replay assumes unique case IDs, fixed reference labels and a current revision whenever the index responds. Separate intake controls found that the archived rule accepts a duplicate that masks a failure and a changed label that matches a wrong prediction. The index can fail to respond in these profiles. This run did not include a successful stale response. One local follow-up checks exact revision matching with a trusted revision in the request. A second obtains that revision from a separate same-owner process and counts pipe payload. Independent operation and production fault isolation remain open. CPU timings are diagnostic. Matched terms: read, stale, separate, revision, must

routes.excerpt: 55.11.1 JEPA is a prediction objective, not a complete agent I-JEPA predicts target-region embeddings from image context using a Transformer predictor and an EMA target encoder. V-JEPA 2 adds an action-conditioned prediction route after video pretraining. LeJEPA instead makes predictive agreement and Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization (SIGReg) central to its collapse-prevention recipe; it avoids the teacher–student and stop-gradient machinery used in several other variants. A model label must therefore resolve the actual objective, view construction, target/predictor state, regularizer and downstream task. An embedding encoder is not a drop-in replacement for a text-generating reasoner or an authorized controller. The 2026 Platonic-representation result makes view construction consequential: its authors report that a 109M text JEPA exceeds evaluated language models through 72B parameters on specified alignment measures. That comparison concerns representation geometry, not general reasoning or task competence. Its theorem is conditional and uses an identity predictor; its practical runs use LeJEPA without exactly meeting the theorem’s hypotheses. Neither result grants this ABI an implementation or qualification.

routes.excerpt: 55.11.1 JEPA is a prediction objective, not a complete agent I-JEPA predicts target-region embeddings from image context using a Transformer predictor and an EMA target encoder. V-JEPA 2 adds an action-conditioned prediction route after video pretraining. LeJEPA instead makes predictive agreement and Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization (SIGReg) central to its collapse-prevention recipe; it avoids the teacher–student and stop-gradient machinery used in several other variants. A model label must therefore resolve the actual objective, view construction, target/predictor state, regularizer and downstream task. An embedding encoder is not a drop-in replacement for a text-generating reasoner or an authorized controller. The 2026 Platonic-representation result makes view construction consequential: its authors report that a 109M text JEPA exceeds evaluated language models through 72B parameters on specified alignment measures. That comparison concerns representation geometry, not general reasoning or task competence. Its theorem is conditional and uses an identity predictor; its practical runs use LeJEPA without exactly meeting the theorem’s hypotheses. Neither result grants this ABI an implementation or qualification.

routes.excerpt: 37.7.3 Clustering the retrieval index An inverted file (IVF) puts embeddings in buckets so a query can search a few likely buckets before ranking the passages inside them. In Euclidean k-means the builder chooses a fixed number of centers, \(k\), and aims to minimize the mean squared distance from each vector to its nearest center. Lloyd’s algorithm assigns all vectors to their nearest center, replaces each center with the mean of its assigned vectors, and repeats. k-means++ spreads out the initial centers by favoring points far from those already chosen. Flash-KMeans speeds up full-batch assignment and reduction on GPUs. SuperKMeans prunes distance calculations and can stop fitting when nearest-neighbor recall stops improving on validation queries. Faiss · k-means++ · Flash-KMeans · SuperKMeans e-means fits the same objective with updates after each mini-batch. Classic mini-batch k-means accumulates a running mean of assigned points. e-means maintains an exponentially decayed sum and count for each center. Their ratio gives the new center, with recent points weighted more heavily. The recipe lowers the update step over the run, revives underused centers by splitting active ones, and sets batch size and initial step from empirical scaling rules. Those rules were fitted for embedding workloads and are weaker defaults on very small or low-dimensional datasets. The labels ret

routes.excerpt: 74.10.8 Neuron-level personality steering and distributed persona control The October Neuron Explorer and Neuronary projects linked from Lyra’s website make a concrete phenomenon accessible: changing a small set of MLP activation coordinates can substantially alter a model’s expressed character, tone and self-description. The linked “Evil Qwen” example is a community demonstration of such a change. It is useful as an intervention lead, without establishing a universal “evil switch,” a new desire or the complete mechanism behind the persona. The earlier research below and the recent tools have distinct contributions and evidence scopes. Three intervention objects are easy to confuse: Raw MLP coordinates. NPTI contrasts activation probabilities under opposing Big Five trait prompts, then suppresses selected coordinates and increases others during inference. “Neuron” names an architectural coordinate at a specified site. It does not imply that one unit contains an entire human personality. Its identification statistic uses the nonlinear gate output, which is not the same signal as the gated product entering down_proj in Lyra’s inspected runtime. Distributed directions.
